hot.pointer_line: On now: Mary Cassatt at the Musée d'Orsay, Remember Me at the Bourse de Commerce and Gustave Fayet at the Fondation Louis Vuitton, Art Basel Paris at the Grand Palais on 23–25 October, clocks back on 25 October, the Salon du Chocolat on 28 October–1 November, Paris Photo on 12–15 November, Beaujolais Nouveau on Thursday 19 November and the Champs-Élysées lights from 22 November, with game, cèpes and oysters in the bistros; the Seine swimming sites are shut until next summer.

groups.title: On the river
groups.desc: The swims are over for the year; the river is for looking at, and for one wine-soaked evening in November.

items.name: The Seine swims: closed until next summer
items.teaser: Bras Marie, Bercy and Grenelle ran 4 July to 30 August 2026; nobody swims in the Seine in October
items.story: For a second summer Paris let people into the Seine at three supervised sites: Bras Marie by the Pont Louis-Philippe in the 4th, Bercy in the 12th and Grenelle in the 15th, free, from 4 July to 30 August 2026. Grenelle shut from 1 to 9 August for the open-water and high-diving events of the 2026 European Aquatics Championships. The season ended a day early: storms kept the sites closed on 29 August, and the city counted 120,000 bathers across the three. There is no swimming now; the next season should come in summer 2027, dates not yet announced.
items.why: Walk the quays at Bras Marie and look at the river instead; save the swim for a July visit.
facts: 2027 dates are not out yet: check paris.fr in spring

items.name: Beaujolais Nouveau on the water
items.teaser: An hour on the Seine from the Pont Neuf with the new gamay poured as you go, around Beaujolais night
items.story: The Vedettes du Pont Neuf, whose boats leave from the square du Vert-Galant at the tip of the Île de la Cité, sell a one-hour Beaujolais Nouveau cruise with the new wine poured without limit, priced on their page at 25 to 27 euros. The page describes it as the weekend of 19 November 2026, but 19 November is a Thursday, the legal release day, so the sailing days need checking before booking. It is the river's one seasonal party: the Louvre, the Musée d'Orsay and Notre-Dame slide past in the early dark while the glasses are filled.
items.why: A cheap way to give guests the Seine and the new vintage in one hour; confirm the sailing date first.
facts: The page's date wording is inconsistent: book only once the day is confirmed

groups.title: In the galleries
groups.desc: The art fair week, a photography week and the season's big museum shows.

items.name: Art Basel Paris, 23–25 October
items.teaser: 206 galleries from 41 countries under the Grand Palais glass roof, with shows spilling across the city
items.story: The fair that replaced the FIAC returns to the restored Grand Palais for its public days on Friday 23 to Sunday 25 October 2026, after an invitation-only Avant-Première on 20 October, preview days on 21 and 22 October and a public vernissage on the 22nd. The organisers list 206 galleries from 41 countries and territories. Around it, the off-site programme runs from 20 to 25 October, with installations in public places and institutions across Paris. For a week the 8th fills with collectors, dealers and their dinners, and the restaurants around the Champs-Élysées know it.
items.why: Book dinner tables near the Grand Palais now; fair week fills them.
facts: Public days Fri 23–Sun 25 Oct 2026; off-site 20–25 Oct
Grand Palais, avenue du Général Eisenhower, 8th
Friday morning is the calmest public slot before the weekend crowd

items.name: Mary Cassatt at the Musée d'Orsay
items.teaser: About 80 works by the American who joined the Impressionists, in the museum's fortieth-birthday season
items.story: The Musée d'Orsay turns forty this season and its lead show is Mary Cassatt, 'Le choix de l'indépendance', from 6 October 2026 to 31 January 2027: about 80 works by the Pittsburgh-born painter who settled in Paris and exhibited with the Impressionists. From 20 October the museum adds Jenny Holzer, 'J'ai vu', running to 21 February 2027, and the Bartholdi show on the Statue of Liberty, open since September, stays to 31 January. The reception areas are under works until summer 2028, so the entrance can move: check the site on the day.
items.why: Pair Cassatt with the Holzer show from 20 October: two independent women, a century apart, in one visit.
facts: Cassatt 6 Oct 2026–31 Jan 2027; Holzer 20 Oct 2026–21 Feb 2027
Museum ticket; book a timed slot online

items.name: Paris Photo, 12–15 November
items.teaser: The world's big photography fair, back under the Grand Palais roof for its 29th edition
items.story: Three weeks after Art Basel the Grand Palais changes medium: Paris Photo holds its 29th edition from Thursday 12 to Sunday 15 November 2026, after a ticketed vernissage on Wednesday 11 November. Listings give opening hours of 13:00 to 20:00, closing at 19:00 on the Sunday. It lines up with a city full of photographs: the Bourse de Commerce is showing 'Remember Me', about 700 works by more than 70 artists from the Pinault Collection, to 18 January 2027, and the Louvre is opening its own photography season.
items.why: Do the fair, then walk to the Bourse de Commerce for the Pinault photographs the same week.
facts: Opens at 13:00: lunch first, fair after

groups.title: On the plate
groups.desc: Game, wild mushrooms and oysters in the bistros, and five days of chocolate at Porte de Versailles.

items.name: Game season in the bistros
items.teaser: Wild game can only be sold in the hunting season, so from now to February it is on the blackboards
items.story: In France wild game may be sold only during the hunting season, which runs from autumn into February; farmed game is around all year. So this is when the bistros write grouse, mallard, hare and venison on the board. Chez L'Ami Jean in the 7th books up for its autumn and winter game, roast grouse and wild boar stew among them. Au Bascou in the 3rd, a South-West bistro, treats lièvre à la royale, hare slow-cooked in its own blood-thickened sauce, as its signature from October to the end of January. The dish is rare and kitchens make it in small batches.
items.why: Ask when you book whether the lièvre à la royale is on: it runs out.
facts: Hunting season, roughly autumn to February
À la carte; game dishes carry a premium
2026 menus are not online yet: ask the restaurant what has come in

items.name: Cèpes, girolles and the R-month oyster
items.teaser: Wild mushrooms peak in October and the oysters are back on the raw bars
items.story: October is when the cèpe is at its best on the Paris stalls, with girolles, chestnuts, squash and quince beside it, and the old R-month rule puts oysters back on every counter. Two rooms on rue de Charonne in the 11th show both sides of it. Septime's menus are driven by the season, and The World's 50 Best has cited its cèpes and girolles in peppercorn sauce. Next door Clamato, Septime's seafood bar, takes no bookings and builds its card on the morning's delivery, with raw-bar oysters and a fruits de mer platter.
items.why: Book Septime weeks out; for Clamato, turn up at opening and queue.
facts: Cèpes at their peak in October; oysters from September

items.name: Salon du Chocolat, 28 October–1 November
items.teaser: The 31st edition fills Hall 5 at Porte de Versailles with chocolatiers and pastry chefs for five days
items.story: The Salon du Chocolat et de la Pâtisserie holds its 31st edition from Wednesday 28 October to Sunday 1 November 2026, after an opening night on Tuesday 27 October from 19:00 to 22:00. It takes Hall 5 at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles, open 10:00 to 19:00 each day. The 2025 edition, the 30th, ran 29 October to 2 November, so the dates stay pinned to the Toussaint week. Expect chocolatiers' stands, pastry demonstrations and tastings; the weekend falls on the 1 November holiday and is the most crowded.
items.why: Go on the Wednesday or Thursday, when tickets are cheaper and the aisles are quieter.
facts: Paris Expo Porte de Versailles, Hall 5
About 16 EUR weekdays, 20 EUR weekends (one listing, seen Oct 2026)
Sunday 1 November is a public holiday: expect the biggest crowd

groups.title: In the calendar
groups.desc: The fixed dates between now and December.

items.name: The clocks go back, Sunday 25 October
items.teaser: At 03:00 on Sunday 25 October the clocks return to 02:00: dusk comes an hour earlier by the clock
items.story: France leaves summer time on the last Sunday of October, as the whole European Union does: on Sunday 25 October 2026, at 03:00, the clocks go back to 02:00 and that Sunday has 25 hours. It is also the last day of Art Basel Paris, so anyone with a morning slot at the Grand Palais gains an hour in bed. From then on the evening light goes an hour earlier by the clock, and a terrace drink at dusk becomes a late-afternoon drink.
items.why: Move sunset drinks and river walks an hour earlier from 25 October.
facts: Phones change by themselves; crew rotas and bookings made in summer do not

items.name: Beaujolais Nouveau, Thursday 19 November
items.teaser: The third Thursday of November: the new gamay goes on sale and the wine bars pour it from opening
items.story: Since a decree of 29 October 1985 the Beaujolais Nouveau has been released on the third Thursday of November, which in 2026 is 19 November. Paris marks it in its bars rather than in any one place; the city's tourism office lists the evening as free to join and names two addresses to taste, La Bonne Franquette at 2 rue des Saules in Montmartre and Les Noces de Jeannette in the 2nd. The wine is young and light, made to be drunk within months, and the fun is the crowd at the counter.
items.why: Go to a wine bar, not a tourist café: the counters with regulars make the night.
facts: Wine bars citywide; e.g. La Bonne Franquette, 18th
Free to join; pay by the glass
Book a bistro table that evening: the good ones fill

items.name: The Champs-Élysées lights, from Sunday 22 November
items.teaser: The avenue's Christmas lights are due on 22 November, with a Christmas market back on the Champs-Élysées
items.story: Two Paris outlets report that the Champs-Élysées Christmas illuminations will be switched on on Sunday 22 November 2026, with the avenue closed to traffic for a reworked launch. The same reports say a Christmas market returns to the avenue for the first time in nearly ten years, open until 4 January 2027. In 2025 the lights went on on Sunday 16 November and stayed up to 4 January. The department-store windows on boulevard Haussmann light up from mid-November. No switch-on hour has been published, and the Ville de Paris has not yet confirmed the date.
items.why: Walk the avenue from the Arc de Triomphe down towards Concorde after dark for the full run of lights.
facts: From Sun 22 Nov 2026 (reported, not yet official); market to 4 Jan 2027
The avenue is closed to traffic for the launch: no car drop-offs that evening

groups.title: Spring: the farm, the marathon, the garden
groups.desc: Rural France comes to town in February, the city runs in April, and the gardens open in June.

items.name: Salon International de l'Agriculture, 27 February–7 March 2027
items.teaser: Nine days when France's cattle, cheeses and charcuterie fill Porte de Versailles
items.story: Once a year rural France moves into the exhibition halls at Porte de Versailles: livestock breeds in their pens, regional produce stands, AOP cheeses and charcuterie to taste, and the politicians who come to be photographed with them. The 2027 edition runs from Saturday 27 February to Sunday 7 March, reported open 9:00 to 19:00, with the Ferrandaise cattle breed and Serbia as guests in one preview. Ticket prices for 2027 had not been published when checked.
items.why: Go on a weekday morning and head for the regional produce halls, not the livestock rings, for the tasting.
facts: Weekends are packed with families: go Monday to Thursday

items.name: Marathon de Paris, Sunday 4 April 2027
items.teaser: The 50th edition, under a new title sponsor, with central streets shut for the morning
items.story: The Paris marathon reaches its 50th edition on Sunday 4 April 2027, reported as the ASICS Marathon de Paris after a change of title partner; some earlier listings gave 11 April, but the reports from September 2026 agree on the 4th. Entry was by lottery, open from 8 to 30 September 2026. The half marathon comes first, on Sunday 7 March 2027. The 2027 course will be published only early in the year, so the closures are not known yet; in past years the race has started on the Champs-Élysées.
items.why: For guests not running, plan a late brunch away from the route rather than trying to cross it.
facts: Citywide; 2027 course to be published early 2027

items.name: Rendez-vous aux jardins, early June
items.teaser: One weekend when public and private gardens across France open their gates, many of them free
items.story: The Ministry of Culture's Rendez-vous aux jardins opens gardens across France for one weekend at the start of June, Paris among them, with private courtyards, ministry gardens and park greenhouses taking part alongside the public parks. Regional listings put the 2027 edition on Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 June, but no national programme had been published when checked, and one listing gives 4–6 June. The Paris programme comes out district by district a few weeks ahead.
items.why: Watch for the Paris list in May and pick the gardens that are normally closed.
facts: Usually the first weekend of June (5–6 Jun 2027 in regional listings)
Some private gardens need booking: check the programme in May

groups.title: Summer: music, the fourteenth and the river
groups.desc: A night of art, a day of free music, the national holiday and the Seine opened for swimming.

items.name: Fête de la Musique, 21 June
items.teaser: On the longest day the whole city becomes the stage, from midday to the small hours
items.story: Every 21 June, the summer solstice, France holds the Fête de la Musique: free concerts by anyone who wants to play, on street corners, in courtyards, café terraces and the city's institutions, in all twenty arrondissements. In 2027 it falls on a Monday, so it is a working day and the crowds come out after work and stay late. The metro runs late that night and many streets become pedestrian. Earlier in June, Nuit Blanche, the free all-night art event, was held on Saturday 6 June in 2026.
items.why: Eat early, then walk; the best sets are the ones you stumble on.
facts: Keep cars away from the centre that evening: walk or take the metro

sources.label: Sortiraparis: Nuit Blanche 2026, Saturday 6 June

items.name: Le Quatorze Juillet
items.teaser: The military parade down the Champs-Élysées in the morning, fireworks at the Eiffel Tower at night
items.story: France's national day, 14 July, keeps its fixed shape in Paris: the military parade on the Champs-Élysées in the morning, and fireworks over the Eiffel Tower and the Trocadéro at night, with the firemen's balls (bals des pompiers) in the fire stations around it. In 2027 the 14th is a Wednesday. Expect the avenue and the area round the Champ de Mars to be closed and searched for hours ahead. The city empties after the holiday, and many owner-run restaurants close for part of the summer.
items.why: Book anything you want in the second half of July before you come; many kitchens shut for the summer.
facts: Security perimeters close early: be in place well before dark for the fireworks

items.name: The Seine swims and Paris Plages
items.teaser: Free supervised swimming in the Seine at three sites, open July and August since 2025
items.story: Since summer 2025 Paris has opened the Seine to swimmers at three supervised sites: Bras Marie by the Pont Louis-Philippe in the 4th, Bercy in the 12th and Grenelle in the 15th. In 2026 they ran free from 4 July to 30 August, Bras Marie from 8:00 to 18:00, Bercy 11:00 to 21:00, Grenelle 10:00 to 17:30, and the city counted 120,000 bathers. Swimming can be stopped when rain degrades the water quality, as it was on 29 August. Paris Plages, the summer beach on the quays, runs over the same weeks. The 2027 dates are not yet announced.
items.why: Bras Marie opens earliest: a morning swim with the Île Saint-Louis across the water.
facts: Sites shut after heavy rain: check the day's status before going

groups.title: Autumn and winter: the harvest, the gamay, the galette
groups.desc: A vineyard festival on the Butte, the new Beaujolais, and the cake of the Epiphany.

items.name: Fête des Vendanges de Montmartre, early October
items.teaser: Paris's own vineyard, the Clos Montmartre, toasts its harvest with five days of parades and tastings
items.story: The Clos Montmartre, replanted in 1933 on the north slope of the Butte, gives only a small harvest, but it has had its festival since 1934. The 93rd edition ran from Wednesday 7 to Sunday 11 October 2026 under a music theme, with the opening night at the 18th arrondissement town hall, the Ban des Vendanges at the vineyard and a parade on the Saturday, and a closing dance in the Square Louise Michel below the Sacré-Cœur. It is free and held each year in the first half of October; the 2027 dates are not yet out.
items.why: Come for the Saturday parade, then eat on the Butte once the crowd has gone down the hill.
facts: The vineyard ceremony is by invitation; the parade and street events are open to all

items.name: Beaujolais Nouveau, the third Thursday of November
items.teaser: Fixed by decree since 1985: Thursday 19 November 2026, Thursday 18 November 2027
items.story: The release day of the Beaujolais Nouveau is set by law: a decree of 29 October 1985 put it on the third Thursday of November. That makes it Thursday 19 November in 2026 and Thursday 18 November in 2027. In Paris it is a bar-counter night rather than a festival in one place, with wine bars and bistros pouring the new gamay from opening time. The wine is made fast from that autumn's harvest and meant to be drunk young, through the winter.
items.why: Pick a wine bar with regulars at the counter; that is where the night happens.
facts: Book a bistro table for that evening

items.name: The galette des rois, January
items.teaser: Puff pastry, frangipane and a hidden fève: every boulangerie sells it through January
items.story: The Epiphany falls on 6 January, a Wednesday in 2027, and in France the feast is usually kept on the first Sunday of January, which in 2027 is the 3rd. The Paris version of the galette des rois is puff pastry filled with frangipane, with a small fève hidden inside: whoever finds it wears the paper crown that comes with the cake. Boulangeries sell it from the turn of the year through most of January, and the youngest at the table traditionally sits under it and calls out who gets each slice.
items.why: Buy it from a real bakery, not a supermarket; the butter shows.
facts: Epiphany Wed 6 Jan 2027; sold through January
Priced by size at each bakery
Order a large one a day ahead from a good bakery in early January
